text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- (Right wing) Disy party vice chairman and candidate for the party leadership Nicos Anastassiades polls 73 percent in an independent survey over 27 percent from challenger Demetris Syllouris.

- A Filipina maid gave birth on her own and left the newborn infant in a cardboard box outside the home she worked at, initially denying it was hers because she was scared her employer would dismiss her.
- Communist Akel will not hesitate to support President Glafcos Clerides at upcoming talks in New York even though presidential elections are coming, says party chief Demetris Christofias.
- Ankara has proposed that accession talks between Cyprus and the European Union be frozen in return for holding off its integration of occupied north Cyprus into Turkey.
- The Auditor-General suggests adopting proper tender proceedures in the electricity authority for projects costing below 200,000 pounds ($395,000).

- The United Nations and foreign mediators on the Cyprus dispute are preparing formulas on basic issues of the Cyprus dispute in view of the scheduled meeting of President Clerides with Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash.
- Insurance companies seek permission to administer provident and pension funds. ($=0.506 pounds)
